transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 00:42:00
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Acme Eng Lead), Marco Rivera (Acme Backend), Priya Nair (Acme PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): quick sync on SDK integration; some flaky structured outputs; need updated examples and a dedicated latency run.

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — samir will go over the SDK updates and the structured output schema, then lena / marco can share the integration blockers, and we'll sync on next steps.
[00:00:18] Lena Ortiz: thanks, maya. we did the initial integration this week, used the JS SDK snippet you sent but ran into a couple issues with function calling payloads and the response shape, so some of our parsing broke.
[00:00:33] Samir Patel: yeah we saw the log you pasted in the slack thread — thanks. so first, important detail: we shipped a small SDK patch last wednesday that changes the function-call representation slightly (we flattened the tool.metadata field). i realize that may have caused your parser to miss nested fields.
[00:00:49] Marco Rivera: right, that matches what we saw — previously we expected tool.metadata.context and now it's tool_meta in some responses? the transcriber had it as tool dot meta, so a little messy.
[00:01:02] Maya Chen: sorry about the churn — i'll put the exact changelog in the follow-up. samir, can you run through recommended parsing approach that's robust to these SDK variations?
[00:01:12] Samir Patel: sure. two pragmatic patterns: 1) rely on the structured_output schema we provided (we added a top-level 'structured' object with exact keys for (intent, entities, actions)). 2) defensively check both tool.metadata and tool_meta fields for backward compatibility. example: in JS, a small wrapper that normalizes the response before feeding into the app. i can paste the snippet.
[00:01:36] Priya Nair: that would be great. also, our product needs deterministic keys for downstream processors — we had unexpected nulls which caused the pipeline to abort.
[00:01:47] Samir Patel: understood — the structured output mode is designed for deterministic outputs. note that if you use the SDK with the streaming option, you might get partial structured outputs until the model finishes; the current SDK will emit an interim 'structured.partial' event — you should only act on structured.complete.
[00:02:10] Marco Rivera: ah, that explains our flaky behavior — we were treating first structured event as final.
[00:02:18] Lena Ortiz: can you show the sample schema again? we had an example in the doc but our devs said it didn't match the actual responses.
[00:02:26] Samir Patel: sure. (shares link) Deck: https://redwood.app/s/acme/poc/structured-output-v2 — the important bits: top-level 'structured' object, fields: intent:string, entities:array, actions:array of {name, params}, and a 'confidence' float. also for tool-calls we use 'tools' array where each tool has 'name', 'arguments' (JSON string or object depending on call style), and 'status'.
[00:02:57] Lena Ortiz: that matches the v2 but not what we saw in staging — staging responses had 'tools' as a map instead of an array sometimes.
[00:03:08] Samir Patel: hmm — that should only happen if you are using older model variants in Hosted. can you confirm the model name and endpoint you hit?
[00:03:18] Marco Rivera: we hit hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate with model: redwood-alpha-1 but our environment variable pointed to the older stable alias redwood-alpha-1@stable. maybe that alias still maps to a prior variant.
[00:03:31] Maya Chen: good catch — aliases can change semantics. i'll check with onboarding infra to confirm alias mapping for that timestamp. in the meantime, samir, would recommending pinning the model version be appropriate?
[00:03:42] Samir Patel: yes, for POC we recommend pinning to a specific model version or variant (we typically provide the commit hash in the SDK call) — that'll make responses deterministic while you validate parsing.
[00:03:55] Priya Nair: linking to production concerns: what about latency — we saw 600-800ms 95th p95 in staging for a 120-token request; is that expected for Hosted?
[00:04:08] Samir Patel: depends on batch windowing, concurrency, and whether KV cache warmed. for small requests, p95 under 400ms is achievable on Dedicated; Hosted can be 300-900ms depending on load. if latency is critical we can run a Dedicated benchmark with your workload to see economics.
[00:04:24] Lena Ortiz: we did see some warm-up effect — first few requests were much slower. is there a way to keep KV cache warm from our side?
[00:04:31] Samir Patel: you can periodically call a light prefix request to keep hot keys alive; also in Dedicated we can lock some model shards to reduce cold starts. i'll include config suggestions.
[00:04:43] Marco Rivera: ok. switching topics to SDK usage — we used the Python SDK for a background job that orchestrates tool calls (payment confirmation, DB write). tool calling seems to be fine but sometimes the 'arguments' field comes as a stringified JSON, sometimes object. is there a recommended pattern?
[00:05:00] Samir Patel: the SDK will return either depending on whether the model returned raw text or if the runtime applied an automatic parse. recommended approach: use the SDK flag parse_tool_args=true to always return objects; if you can't set that, normalize by trying JSON.parse and fallback to string parsing. i'll add a helper util in the sample.
[00:05:19] Priya Nair: perfect. about structured output validation — can we have Redwood do a short eval run against our golden prompts to measure regression?
[00:05:28] Maya Chen: yes — our Optimize team can run a quality check. samir, can you coordinate what sample prompts they need?
[00:05:35] Samir Patel: i'll need a set of 30-50 representative prompts with expected structured output and a small rubric. if you send those to samir.patel@redwood.ai i'll queue the eval and return a quick report.
[00:05:47] Marco Rivera: we'll compile and send by end of day friday.
[00:05:52] Lena Ortiz: security question — we need SOC2 + KMS key usage for staging logs. we already asked via Zendesk but want to confirm timeline.
[00:06:01] Maya Chen: yes, we previously shared SOC2 and our PKI/KMS docs. i'll reattach the secure link; i'll also ask our security engineer to confirm KMS options for Private deployments if you want to test on-prem later.
[00:06:13] Priya Nair: great. can you share the link now?
[00:06:16] Maya Chen: link: https://redwood.app/security/acme-poc-sso (note: internal access control applies).
[00:06:26] Marco Rivera: thanks. quick question on rollout: we want canary behavior where if the structured parser fails, we fall back to a simpler text parse endpoint — is that a pattern you support?
[00:06:36] Samir Patel: yes — we recommend canary with automatic fallback: route by policy to primary model, if structured.complete not returned within X ms or error code observed, fallback to the text-only endpoint. we have a sample routing policy in the console and a small SDK helper.
[00:06:52] Lena Ortiz: and can we test that policy in Hosted before moving to Dedicated?
[00:06:57] Maya Chen: absolutely — we can configure a canary at route level in Hosted and simulate failures.
[00:07:05] Marco Rivera: noted. on another note, we observed a couple of mis-attributions in the audio logs of the harness — not relevant to product but i flagged in the ticket.
[00:07:14] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll look.
[00:07:20] [00:20:00] (middle of call, detailed debug session)
[00:20:05] Samir Patel: demoing a short JS example now — paste snippet:
const res = await Redwood.generate({
  model: 'redwood-alpha-1@2026-11-10',
  structured_output: true,
  parse_tool_args: true,
  functions: [{ name: 'charge_customer', schema: { amount: 'number', currency: 'string', id: 'string' } }],
});
// normalize
const structured = normalize(res.structured);
if (structured.complete) { callLocalFunction(structured.actions); }
[00:20:32] Marco Rivera: good — can you add the error handler example when parsing fails?
[00:20:37] Samir Patel: yep will add. gist link: https://redwood.app/code/acme/js-sdk-examples
[00:20:45] Priya Nair: also we need an example of the webhook flow when a tool is called and returns async result.
[00:20:51] Samir Patel: we have that — it's in the app-integration section, shows how to wait for tool.status == 'completed' and reconcile with idempotency keys.
[00:21:00] Lena Ortiz: thanks. small perf question: when we enable structured_output the cost went up ~10% in our preliminary numbers — expected?
[00:21:08] Samir Patel: structured_output adds a small parsing/compute step; we typically see 5-15% overhead depending on model and sequence length. you can reduce cost by using a lighter variant for parsing or quantized Dedicated config — i'll add the quantization suggestion as an action item.
[00:21:24] Maya Chen: we should also map the expected token delta for your prompts — samir, can you estimate?
[00:21:29] Samir Patel: if your prompts average 90 tokens, structured output may add 30-60 tokens for the schema and metadata. we'll provide a more exact token profile after the eval.
[00:21:40] Marco Rivera: ok. final items — we want to run a 2-hour Dedicated benchmark with our real traffic pattern to evaluate p95 and cost; can redwood support that?
[00:21:50] Samir Patel: yes, we can set up a reserved short-term Dedicated cluster or run a synthetic load in Hosted with matching concurrency. prefer Dedicated for accurate economics. i'll coordinate with capacity — may need a week lead.
[00:21:59] Priya Nair: timeline: we'd like results before our internal review on 2026-12-10.
[00:22:05] Maya Chen: noted — samir will aim to schedule the benchmark the week of 11/30 to 12/6.
[00:22:11] [00:35:00] (wrap-up)
[00:35:05] Maya Chen: quick recap: 1) Maya to share SDK sample + changelog and SOC2/KMS link by 11/27. 2) Samir to add normalization utils, canary routing sample, and a Dedicated config suggestion (including quantization) by 12/01. 3) Acme to run staging integration tests and send prompts/golden outputs by 12/02. 4) Schedule Dedicated benchmark week of 11/30 (Samir + Marco).
[00:35:35] Lena Ortiz: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[00:35:39] Marco Rivera: thanks.
[00:35:42] Priya Nair: thanks, bye.

References/shared artifacts noted in call:
- SDK snippets (JS/Python): https://redwood.app/code/acme/js-sdk-examples
- Structured output v2 deck: https://redwood.app/s/acme/poc/structured-output-v2
- Security docs link (SOC2/KMS): https://redwood.app/security/acme-poc-sso

End of transcript.
